label: No mutual necessary support, from actual well-foundedness and no novel edge
description: Prices the mutual-support rival of J2: with reflexive access at w and well-founded actual grounding at w (both premises of the join the rival was tested against), the rival is incompatible with the one-way no-novel-edge condition. A holder of the rival who accepts the join's other premises must therefore posit a support edge between two necessary concreta that holds at some admitted world of the carrier but not at w. That world may be inaccessible from w, so this is not by itself modal contingency of support relative to w. A conditional exclusion; neither the condition nor the rival is established or refuted.

research_comparisons.conditions: mutualSupportExcluded: ActualReflexive m.ontic w, ActualGroundingWF m w and NoNovelNecessarySupport on the concrete subtype at w give the negation of NecessaryConcretaMutualSupport m w.
research_comparisons.scope: Same Profile, selected relation and selected world as the premise and the rival; any worlds and carrier.
research_comparisons.coverage: All interpretations satisfying the three listed premises.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: The exclusion holds only under the no-novel-edge condition, which is open and stronger than J2 given the other two premises; without it the rival survives (Control.mutualPair, Control.rootedPair).
research_comparisons.next_step: Assess the warrant of the no-novel-edge condition; none is recorded. An essence-based account of support between necessary beings is only an unformalised analyst sketch: as sketched it is a two-way invariance, stronger than no-novel-edge, and its use toward coverage needs F1. The rival's world-varying shape simply denies such an account. Mere loss of actual edges at other worlds does not violate no-novel-edge.
